title: Effects of architectural interventions on psychological, cognitive, social, and pro-environmental aspects of occupant well-being: Results from an immersive online study

findings.mechanism: windows allow occupants to experience views of nature, connecting them to the outside environment, which promotes a stronger sense of belonging. This effect was maintained after controlling for covariates.
findings.quote: participants exposed to windows reported higher belonging scores (p < 0.001***) than those in the no window conditions

findings.mechanism: In the natural materials condition, diverse representation leads to higher belonging scores. This interaction effect was maintained after controlling for covariates.
findings.quote: In the natural materials condition, diverse representation leads to higher (p = 0.05*) belonging scores

findings.mechanism: In the artificial materials condition, diverse representation led to lower perceived belonging compared to non-diverse representation. However, this interaction loses significance after running post-hoc tests with outliers excluded.
findings.quote: perceived belonging is higher (p = 0.02*) in the presence of non-diverse representation (M = 5.21, SD = 1.07) compared to in the diverse representation condition (M = 4.81, SD = 1.33)

findings.mechanism: In the non-diverse condition, belonging scores were higher when artificial materials were present compared to natural materials. This effect was maintained after controlling for covariates.
findings.quote: in the non-diverse condition, belonging scores were higher (p = 0.017*) when artificial materials were also present

stimuli.description: multiple pictures of an indoor space, full view of the condition as survey background, close-up of framed photographs on walls (diverse vs. non-diverse people)
40-s panoramic video of the assigned indoor space condition

tables.description: Mean and standard deviation of measured dependent variables in each level of independent variable.
ANOVA results with outliers included, showing F-statistics, p-values, and effect sizes (generalized eta squared) for main effects and interactions of independent variables on dependent variables.

limitations: Researchers cannot control the actual built environment in which participants take the survey (e.g., a participant in a windowless condition might be in a room with natural light).
Additional real-world characteristics (e.g., ambient sounds, presence of other people) might confound variables in an online experiment.
Online studies are not well suited for testing tactile and olfactory aspects of the built environment.
Photographs cannot fully reproduce the biological benefits of true natural light or negative effects like glare/thermal discomfort from windows.
Small effect sizes might be due to limited exposure duration (<1 hour) to built features.
The study used only two levels for each independent variable (e.g., presence vs. absence of windows), and future work should investigate the quantity of such elements.
